title: Siena, Concistoro 2308 fasc. 2 'Lettere in cifra': the unread pieces (1421 letter not photographed; nos. 7, 9, 11, 15, 17, 19, 21, R4794)

steps.what: Found the whole busta Concistoro 2308 on DECODE (keys R4746-R4789, letters R4790-R4814, R1858), missed by the 23 Sept scan; downloaded 131 images with the project cookie.
Inventoried fasc. 2 by the pencil numbers (Meister's numbering: no. 4 = 1456, no. 11 = 1478, no. 17 = 1528 hold). Nos. 1 (the 1421 letter), 2, 26-28 are not among the 25 pieces photographed.

Viewed and indexed the 43 key records (1433 Petrucci, c. 1440 frate Bernardino, 1454 Milan ambassadors, Casole, 1478 Bichi, c. 1500 Valentino/Pandolfo keys, 1502, 1536, 1540s Tosta, 16th-c. code books).
Transcribed the unnumbered all-cipher slip R4794 (170 tokens, 38 glyphs, numbers 44, 26, 67, 74 as code groups) from an automatic glyph-segmentation sheet.
Homophonic simulated annealing (homsolve.py, it-cinquecento and la order-4 LMs, unigram KL prior) on R4794: no convergence, restarts disagree.

Checked the alphabets of the 16th-c. keys R4760 (1536), R4765, R4767 (Aglo Venturi), R4768 (Mercanto, lowercase-letter cipher with nulls e g f h k 8 6), R4775 (1502), R4778, R4779, R4785 against nos. 17, 20 and R4794: no match seen.

No. 20 (R4808) transcribed by a subagent: 1,231 tokens, 51 sign names, continuous; clear opening 'Sacra Regia Maiestas ... ante terre pedum oscula', closing 'Scriptum Perusii(?) die penultimo mensis Martii'.
No. 20: homsolve.py Italian/Latin, with and without f/o^n as nulls, and with f as word divider; homsolve2.py Latin: no convergence.
No. 11 (Acciaiuoli 1478, 409 tokens, 44 signs, 'PLUS O' merged): homophonic anneal Italian, no convergence.
No. 23 (R4811) fully transcribed by two subagents: 54 lines, 3,703 tokens; clear 'como vi dirrò' inside the cipher (Italian).

No. 17 (1528, 282 tokens): homsolve2 Italian 40 restarts; best runs throw up 'pitiliano', 'questo', 'cardinal', 'pratica' but no coherent text; crib Pitiliano fixed: no convergence (too short for 40+ signs).
Keys with digit+letter alphabets tested against no. 17: R4778 (c. 1500, 6 = c) contradicts no. 17's commonest sign 6 (a vowel); R4760 (1536), R4768 do not fit.
Gabbrielli key volume I index (Ilardi reel 58, index frames): Acciaioli keys only 1504-1514; no key for Donato Acciaiuoli 1478 (no. 11).

No. 20 + no. 23 (4,900 tokens): homsolve2 Italian/Latin/Catalan/Spanish, order 3-4-5, with f-groups (f o^n, f a, f o) merged as units, with superscripted signs as nulls, with o as null: no convergence.
Bigram-capable solver (sylsolve.py: a sign may stand for a letter or one of 40 Italian bigrams), validated on a synthetic cipher, run on nos. 6, 24 and 23: no convergence.
No. 15 (Bandini 1546-47, 229 tokens): key R4764 (Buoninsegni, orator to His Majesty) transcribed (keys/R4764.txt); partial shape mapping + solver: inconclusive (too short to fill the unmapped signs).

Split under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): nos. 25, 18, 14 and 4 moved to their own entries (siena25, siena18, siena14, borghesi1456) with their transcriptions, keys, readings and validation; nos. 6 and 24 left to George Lasry's siena1431. This entry keeps the unread pieces (nos. 7, 9, 11, 15, 17, 19, 20, 21, 23, R4794) as attempted, open, with no shared-key claim; the pieces read at the time (nos. 8, 10, 13/16, 22) and no. 12 are described in NOTES, not counted.

Deduplicated under the one-key rule after George Lasry's contribution siena2023 (PR #41): nos. 20 and 23 (R4808, R4811), one system, removed from this entry's documents, gaps, page and ledgers; this folder's transcriptions and solver inputs for them (transcripts/no20*, no23*) moved to targets/siena2023/project_attempt/. The earlier failed solver steps on them are kept above as the record. This entry now keeps nos. 7, 9, 11, 15, 17, 19, 21 and R4794 unread, and no. 1 (1421) and nos. 2, 26-28 unphotographed.
Downloaded R4797 (no. 8, image I27940) with the DECODE cookie; it was never fetched in September.

No. 8 (R4797): aligned the cipher slip with the clear memorandum above it. The slip is the tail of a letter, clear and cipher mixed; its clear lead words 'Anchora d(iss)e' and 'anti(ve)duto questo' are the memorandum's underlined heads, and three cipher passages fit the memorandum letter by letter with consistent homophones: '(÷) 59t95 75□ø I2 7øϕϕ2 9ff2ϕ +c5' = '[el duca di Milano] aveva dato la donna biancha' (aveva = ABCBA), 'I2ɷ+ctɱt' = 'marchese' twice, 'o-tɷɷ2ɷ2' = 'ferrara', 't ϕøϕ ff9ø I2ϕ+c2 ot +ct' = 'e non può manchare che'. The memorandum is the contemporary decipherment: read at the time, against George Lasry's 'possible but speculative'.

No. 17: George Lasry's key table (signs cut from the manuscript) matched by shape and count to our sign names (transcripts/no17.txt, agent A, 24 Sept); our 283 tokens deciphered with it and aligned with his reading: 252 agree (89.0%) with the first identification, 263 (92.9%) after re-identifying three signs by count (our 7 = his open A, SS = his P '+δ', 5o = his T); the rest fall on his own uncertain words ('el Mustetto', 'Otto', 'lco[..]stren').

No. 11: his key on our transcription (agent B): 66.7% with 8 signs unidentified, 94.4% (357/378 sign units) once his two-stroke signs '+o' = e and 'o+' = d are read as our token pairs PLUS O / O PLUS and ODAG = h, D = a, RHO = o; his nulls 'g#', '31', '87', m^n, /// are our G HASH, 3 1, 8^dot 7, M^n, SL3. Our two cipher blocks are his two runs line for line.

R4794 (his 'no. 5'): his key on our 24 Sept transcription: 83.8% (134/160); his table has no H and no R column though his reading has h 7 times and r 11 times; our A aligns with r every time and N with h; with those two values 93.1% (149/160).

No. 20 (now siena2023): our independent transcription (agent C, 1,230 tokens, other sign names) aligned with his reading by EM from his key values for the sign names both transcriptions share: 71.1% of our tokens carry the majority letter of their sign (78.6% allowing two letters for signs our names merge). Control, his no. 23 plaintext against the same tokens: 14.8% / 23.0%. Our transcription carries his reading.

outcome.method_basis: No filed key of fasc. 1 fits any of these pieces; ciphertext-only homophonic and null-aware solvers fail on the short pieces.
outcome.fraction_read_source: No sign of these pieces has a value.

outcome.notes: Attempted, open for this project: the unread pieces of Concistoro 2308 fasc. 2. Split on 14 Oct 2026; nos. 20 and 23 moved to siena2023 (George Lasry) on 18 Oct 2026. George Lasry's 18 Oct 2026 solutions of R4794, nos. 9, 11, 12, 13, 15 (part) and 17 are outside solutions, recorded in NOTES and checked on 20 Oct 2026 against this folder's transcriptions (verify_lasry.py); no. 8 confirmed as deciphered at the time.
